biography.plain_text: Yevgeniy Strzhalkovskiy is a Russian-born wine entrepreneur based in Monaco. He owns the Piedmont producer Scarpa and founded the Burgundy wine merchant Maison Eugène René. His businesses combine vineyards, cellars and wine tourism, including guest accommodation in the Barolo area. He has also held a controlling interest in a British rum company.

long_biography.plain_text:
Wine entrepreneur Yevgeniy Strzhalkovskiy trained in law and learned winemaking through conversations with producers including Henri Boillot and Carlo Castino. At Scarpa, he faced the costly decision to sell acquired cellar stocks in bulk and replace dolcetto vines with barbera better suited to the soil. He also reserved part of each successful vintage for prolonged ageing.

Outside wine, he has organised historical medieval combat in Monaco. As president of the local association, he presented awards at Buhurt Prime in 2019, where teams fought in reconstructed armour with blunted weapons. He later founded the Magna Carta project, whose Malizia tournament brought European teams to Monaco's big top.
